newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Ousted Ranariddh seeks Manila understanding.
newsitem.headline: Ousted Ranariddh seeks Manila understanding.

text.p: Ousted Cambodian co-premier Prince Norodom Ranariddh asked for the Philippines' "understanding" of his position after he arrived in Manila on Sunday to seek diplomatic support, officials said.

On the day Ranariddh flew in from Bangkok on the fifth leg of his tour of countries in the Association of South East Asian Nations (ASEAN), forces loyal to Second Prime Minister Hun Sen bombarded approaches to the Cambodian town of O'Smach, the last major royalist stronghold.
Ranariddh held more than one hour of talks with Philippine foreign undersecretary Rodolfo Severino and gave an assessment of the situation in his country, Severino told Reuters.
"He wants to put his viewpoint across," Severino said, adding, "What I can say is he was pretty realistic about things."

Severino said Ranariddh sought "understanding about the situation according to his lights," but the Philippine official declined to give specifics, saying only that "all kinds of ideas were being bandied about".
Ranariddh is to meet with President Fidel Ramos on Monday.
"I think what he will do is he will talk about his view of things and see whether the Philippines agrees," Severino said, when asked about what Ranariddh would discuss with Ramos.

"I'll see you after my meeting with the president," the prince told reporters on arrival from Bangkok. He received a low-key welcome at Manila airport from a Philippine official party led by foreign office chief of protocol, Ambassador Victor Garcia.
Ranariddh has previously visited Indonesia, Thailand, Singapore and Malaysia.
ASEAN was to have accepted Cambodia as a member last month but the group postponed its entry after Hun Sen ousted Ranariddh in a coup.
ASEAN comprises Indonesia, the Philippines, Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand, Brunei, Vietnam and new members Laos and Burma.
Officials said Ranariddh might leave Manila on Monday night but did not say where he was headed next.
